- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or mixed), model often fails to correct quickly — apply smoothing or use 3-5 day moving average for mid-term forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted average of last 7–10 days for calibration.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of negative sentiment.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or declining — cap upward bias at 1.5–2.0% above recent mean unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
